names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 7 august, «Sfântul Cuvios Mucenic Dometie Persul», with the rank words left off.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 7 Αυγούστου, «Άγιος Δομέτιος ο Πέρσης και οι δύο μαθητές του», with the rank words and the epithets left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue’s first heading for the Julian 7 August, „Преп. муч. Дометије.“ — Преп. муч. left off, which §5 maps to `venerable-martyr`. The heading gives no ethnonym and no city, so the bare forename is the whole of the form; «the Persian» in the display name is the corpus’s own, off the Romanian «Dometie Persul», and Persia is in the body. `.tmp/sr-foldpred.mjs` reports it folds with nothing, although nine other folders share the Greek Δομέτιος.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 7 august — «Sfântul Cuvios Mucenic Dometie Persul»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 7ης Αυγούστου — «Άγιος Δομέτιος ο Πέρσης και οι δύο μαθητές του»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 7 Αυγούστου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries. It is the same man: a Persian of the years of Constantine the Great, taught the faith by a Christian named Αβαρος, who fled his household, shut himself up in a monastery at Nisibis, went on to Theodosioupolis and the monastery of Sergius and Bacchus, refused the presbyterate the superior Ουρβέλ wished to give him, and was stoned with two disciples in a cave by order of Julian the Apostate. The two disciples are named by no word of the page — «δύο μαθητές του» and nothing further — so they are an unenumerated pair and take no folder of their own. The page gives no year, so the folder's `dates` are untouched; it places the man by three houses rather than one, so no `locations` object is proposed. He is a separate man from `dometios-of-philotheou`, the sign-bearer, whom this same listing carries as its own entry on this same day. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page, which was grepped for there. The page prints one apolytikion and no kontakion, and that apolytikion names him and his pair of disciples, «σὺν φοιτητῶν σου τὴ δυάδι», so it is taken here and not split.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 20.08.2026 (7. август ст. ст.) — „Преп. муч. Дометије.“

attestations.note: The day’s first of five entries, and the Romanian and Greek both keep him on this same 7/8. His row was `undocumented`. **A YEAR ON A FOLDER THAT HELD NO DATE AT ALL.** „Тако сконча овај Божји светитељ 363 год. и пресели се у царство Божје.“ — so this saint of God ended in 363 and passed over to the kingdom of God — is written as `death` 363, flat, basis traditional. **Neither doxologia nor saint.gr gave this folder a year**, and this is the first it has held. The reign in „Када дође у те пределе Јулијан Одступник, чу за Дометија, па посла људе, који га зазидаше у пећини жива са два његова ученика.“ is Julian the Apostate’s and the 363 sits inside it, which is corroboration and not a second reading. **`types` UNTOUCHED, AND EVERY RANK WORD IN THE ENTRY IS ALREADY THERE OR REFUSED.** Преп. муч. is `venerable-martyr` and the folder has it. „Старац Нурвел га зађакони, па када га хтеде принудити и у чин свештеника, Дометије одбеже у неку пустињску гору, и настани се у једној пештери.“ has the elder Nurvel ordain him deacon and then try to force the priesthood on him, at which he fled to a desert mountain: `deacon` is on the folder already from the other two books, and it is a body word here, so the heading adds nothing and nothing is taken away. замонаши се in „Толико заволи веру истиниту, да напусти све светско, и замонаши се у једном манастиру код града Нисивије.“ would give `monk`, which is likewise there already and likewise a body word. **`presbyter` is NOT written**: the entry has him refuse the rank and run, so the one rank the book nearly gives him is the one it denies him. **NO `related` ROW ADDED.** `constantine-the-great` and `dometius-8-march` were `related` here before this reading. „Рођен у Персији као незнабожац, у време цара Константина.“ puts his birth in Persia in the time of Constantine, which is an emperor named to date a life and is not what that row rests on; nothing is added. **The archimandrite Нурвел takes nothing** — `ls saints | grep -iE "^nurvel|nurbel"` returns nothing, so Ruling 3 names him here, and he is the one man in this entry whose own story the entry tells, sixty years without eating anything cooked. The two disciples walled up alive with him are unnamed, which the Greek line this folder already carries also says. No `locations`: Nisibis is named in a clause. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion: the day carries the verse only, which is Bishop Nikolai’s own and belongs to no person.

hymns.text: Cu pustnicia mai înainte pedepsindu-te în munte, taberele vrăjmaşilor cele netrupeşti cu arma Crucii le-ai pierdut, întru tot fericite şi iarăşi spre chinuire bărbăteşte te-ai întrarmat, ucigând pe Copronim cu sabia credinţei. Iar pentru acestea ai fost încununat de Dumnezeu, Cuvioase Mucenice Dometie, pururea mărite.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfântului Cuvios Mucenic Dometie Persul», Glasul 4 — the page names Copronymus, the eighth-century emperor, in a hymn to a fourth-century martyr; the reading is the source's own and is copied as printed

english.text: Having first schooled yourself by the desert life on the mountain, you destroyed the bodiless camps of the enemy with the weapon of the Cross, all-blessed one; and you armed yourself manfully again for the contest, slaying Copronymus with the sword of faith. For this you were crowned by God, venerable martyr Dometius, ever-glorified.

hymns.text: Τὸν τῆς χάριτος λόγον εἰσποιησάμενος, πυρσολατρῶν τᾶς τερθρείας ἀπεποιήσω σοφῶς, τῷ Χριστῷ ἀνατεθεῖς Πάτερ Δομέτιε, καὶ ἐν ἀθλήσει ἀκλινής, ὡς ὁσίων μιμητής, ἐδείχθης Ὁσιομάρτυς, διὸ σὲ ὕμνοις τιμῶμεν, σὺν φοιτητῶν σου τὴ δυάδι σοφέ.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος πλ. α’, Τὸν συνάναρχον Λόγον — the one hymn on the page of «Άγιος Δομέτιος ο Πέρσης και οι δύο μαθητές του», and it names him and the pair of disciples with him

english.text: Having made the word of grace your own, you wisely put away the mummery of the fire-worshippers and were offered up to Christ, father Dometios; and unbending in the contest, as an imitator of the venerable ones, you were shown a venerable martyr. Therefore we honour you with hymns, wise one, together with the pair of your disciples.

death.note: The folder held no date: neither doxologia nor saint.gr gives it a year. The Охридски пролог for 7. август ст. ст.: „Тако сконча овај Божји светитељ 363 год. и пресели се у царство Божје.“ — so this saint of God ended in 363 and passed over to the kingdom of God. The same entry has him walled up alive by men sent by Julian the Apostate, whose reign contains that year and is not used to widen or narrow it (6 October 2026).
